title: An Economic Constitution of Possibility: Producing Real Freedom, Settling Contributions, and Renewing Authority

additional_titles.title: 可能性的经济宪法: 真实自由的生产、贡献的清算与权力的续约

description: What kind of life an income can buy depends on whether services exist, whether routes of access are open, and whether people can refuse the controls that providers attach to them. Taking the results on real exit, the settlement of responsibilities, and continuing renewal in The Canonical Society Theorem, together with its normative argument, as its starting point, this paper extends constitutional scrutiny to all public and private control that affects other people's feasible futures. It develops four institutional entitlements, each requiring separate justification: basic participation rests on human needs and equal standing; contribution claims rest on undertakings accepted in advance; the use of scarce resources is subject to actual budgets and public allocation rules; and governance powers rest on continuing authorization. Beneficiaries, service providers, and those responsible for budgets may be different people. Basic participation therefore requires no prior contribution, while provision must still be delivered through real resources. Eight principles connect capability evaluation, innovation finance, public production, and revocable governance: identical capability readouts may require different repairs; two rounds of exploration under uncertainty can each pay their costs while preserving an old debt; cumulative receipts for one contribution cannot regenerate through transfer; reusing a method can save labor while preserving every previously legal action; and public responsibilities can continue while an existing term of office ends on schedule. Within the given menu and evaluation scope, policy comparison covers every permitted adaptive response: when an acceptable candidate exists, it returns a deployable choice that is no worse across the full responsibility profile; otherwise, it retains the reasons for rejecting each candidate. The actual work of search and verification is charged item by item. The paper thus develops the economic constitution through institutional relationships that can be checked: who pays, who receives a share, who can leave, and who may decide the next rules. Debates in the capability approach, constitutional economics, and polycentric governance are carried forward through these concrete relationships.

additional_descriptions.description: 收入能够购买什么生活，取决于服务是否存在、通路是否开放，以及人能否拒绝提供者附加的控制。本文以《典范社会总定理》关于真实退出、责任清算和持续更新的结果及其规范论述为起点，将经济宪法的审查对象推进到一切影响他人可行未来的公共与私人控制。全文围绕四项须分别说明理由的制度资格展开：基础参与依据人的需要与平等地位，贡献索偿依据事前认可的承担，稀缺使用受实际预算与公开分配规则约束，治理权限依据持续授权。受益者、服务提供者和预算承担者可以不同，因而基础参与无需先有贡献，供给仍须由真实资源兑现。本文通过八项原则连接能力评价、创新融资、公共生产和可撤治理：相同能力读数可能需要不同修复；两轮未知探索可以分别支付成本并保留旧债；一份贡献的累计受领不能因转让而再生；方法复用可以节省劳动并保留所有既有合法行动；公共责任可以继续而旧任期按期结束。在给定菜单与评价范围内，政策比较完整覆盖允许的自适应回应：有可接受候选时返回完整责任非劣的可部署选择，否则逐项保留拒绝理由；实际搜索与核验逐项计费。本文据此将经济宪法落实到可检查的制度关系：谁付款，谁取得份额，谁能离开，谁有权决定下一次规则；能力论、宪制经济学与多中心治理的争论，也由这些具体关系继续展开。

Version 2 revises the bilingual main paper for continuity, institutional interpretation, and scholarly dialogue.
